Players

Every profiled player in the selected mode — click a name to open their profile, or any header to sort. The # column is their standing in this mode.

How the standing is earned

On each hero, a player's result is the share of the other tracked players on that hero they finish above: 7th of 36 beats 29 of the other 35. The standing averages that share across their heroes, trusting a hero more when there are more players to beat on it (up to six) and when the player has more games on it.

That average is then pulled toward the middle of the board by how much evidence backs it, so a broad, well-played record leads when two records are close — and a thin record is only ever held back from the top, never pushed below a worse one.

Avg finish is the same share as a plain average, printed as where they usually place: Top 11% is ahead of 89% of each hero's players, 1st is first on every hero. The standing is an exact place: an exact tie breaks on Avg finish. A — instead of a place means too little evidence to rank yet, not a low rank.

Teammate synergy

Who wins together, at every stack size — toggle Duo / Trio / Quad / 5-stack / 6-stack above. Games and win rate together per mode, and Lift — the group's actual win rate minus the rate expected from the members' records outside the group (in points, ± its own error; descriptive, not causal: stacks also choose when and against whom they queue). No Lift here beats chance: none of the 1,265 survives a 5% false-discovery test across its own table, so none takes a colour — read the column as what these games did, not as chemistry. Click a group's row (▸) to drill in: Hero combos (each member's hero that match, one column per player) or Maps — click a member's name to go straight to their profile instead.

How to read these tables

Groups need 5+ shared games to appear, and a mode shows — until it has 5 games of its own; Lift needs 10+ (a stricter floor — a 5-game sample is too thin for its own shrink to fully tame). Bars, printed rates and sorting all use the raw rate; hover a rate for its sample-shrunk twin (short lucky runs discounted), and * marks modes under 20 games.

Each Lift's ± is one standard error, and it counts the noise in what the members win apart as well as the group's own. A Lift takes a colour only when it survives a 5% false-discovery test across its own stack size's table — the test the hero pages use — so a grey one, however large, is inside what chance alone produces over that many rows.

Sizes overlap in these tables (unlike the stack-size pills above them, where each team counts once at its exact size — so a match where tracked players faced each other reads once for each side, and none of those sizes separates from the solo baseline once you account for how few games the deeper stacks have): a group's games count every match those players shared a team, so a 6-stack's games also appear in every duo, trio, quad and 5-stack inside it.

The Best hero pairings section further down has its own Lift column: same idea, different comparison — a hero PAIR against what the two heroes' other duo line-ups add up to, not a player group against the average of its members' records apart.

In the drilldown, hero line-ups that occurred only once roll up into a one-off tally below the table.

Win rate by stack size — each team counted once, at its exact size. 1 of 5 separate from the solo baseline at the bar a family of 5 needs; the rest are inside their own noise.

The squad's winningest line-ups, from each hero's side — click a hero (▸) for every partner hero two tracked players fielded with it (10+-game pairings; a pairing appears under both its heroes). In the drilldown, Lift weighs each pairing against what its two heroes add up to in their other duo line-ups, and none of its 1,076 pairings beats chance across the section.

Squad matchups

The squad's record when the enemy team fields a hero (each enemy at their primary hero that match), QM + Competitive, over 1,150,223 hero-encounters. Baseline: the squad wins 49.7% of these; the 56 heroes span 14.7pp, from Ultron 43.6% 12,765g up to Black Widow 58.3% 9,468g. Per player these gaps are luck — only 1 of 5,246 gaps survives a 5% false-discovery correction, which is why player pages don't show them — but this spread is far too large and too deep to be chance.

Two caveats that the size of the numbers does not remove. Counting grain: a lobby is folded once per tracked player in it, so a stacked match counts several times — the counts are inflated and the rows are correlated (the rates are unaffected in expectation). Descriptive, not causal: who the enemy picks tracks map, mode and rank band, so a low row says the squad tends to lose lobbies that hero shows up in — not that the hero counters them. Rows under 100 encounters are omitted; hover a Win % for its sample-shrunk rate. Click a hero to open its page.

Squad record book

Group-level bests over the squad's stored history — every match with a tracked player counts once, whoever played (148,871 stored matches; a floor of the true total). A day runs from the group's quietest hour, early morning Eastern, not from midnight, so a late session counts toward its evening. Under the day and stretch cards the QM/Comp line splits that same window by mode and adds back to it; under the two streak cards it is each mode's own longest run, which can be longer than the all-modes streak above it because the other mode's games are skipped rather than breaking it. "Best" day/stretch are ranked by win rate (shrunk toward 50% for small samples), not raw win count — a losing record can never win either slot; the W–L shown is always the real, unshrunk record.
